Strait of Hormuz traffic is picking up after 111 days of near-total gridlock, following the signing of a U.S.-Iran deal, according to CBS News. More tankers are now transiting the waterway, which under normal conditions carries roughly one-fifth of global oil supply. The agreement ends the immediate standoff, but CBS notes that Iran and the U.S. still have significant outstanding issues to negotiate - meaning the current calm is provisional at best.

One IDF soldier was also killed in a Hezbollah IED explosion, according to the Jerusalem Post, a reminder that the wider regional picture has not fully stabilized alongside the Iran diplomacy.

Whether tanker traffic returning to normal translates into sustained de-escalation - or simply a pause before the next pressure point - depends almost entirely on how the remaining negotiations unfold.

How Trump’s immigration crackdown turned detention into a death sentence 

Trump's deportation machine is killing detainees at more than double the rate seen under previous administrations, a bombshell Reuters investigation has revealed. Between 2009 and 2024, immigration centers recorded one death for every 3,848 detainees per year — but since Trump seized power again, that grim statistic has skyrocketed to one death per 1,630 people. And that's just the tip of the iceberg. Internal ICE records obtained by the Deportation Data Project show that 21 of the 50 deaths — including 10 suicides — were only discovered after the detainee had already died or slipped into unconsciousness, raising horrifying questions about whether guards are even bothering to check on the people in their custody. Medical experts who reviewed the autopsy files for Reuters are sounding the alarm, warning that the surge in deaths points to a systemic collapse in oversight and healthcare at overcrowded facilities packed to the brim under Trump's harsh immigration crackdown. 🖥 French FM expresses full support for Islamabad MoU in call with Araghchi

📌 Tehran, IRNA – French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot has expressed Paris’s complete support for the diplomatic process and the resulting memorandum of understanding (MoU) between Iran and the United States.

During the phone call with Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on Thursday, Barrot emphasized France’s full support for the diplomatic process and the resulting MoU, emphasizing the importance of taking advantage of this opportunity to enhance peace, stability, and sustainable security in the region.
​
Meanwhile, the top Iranian diplomat highlighted the importance of the Islamabad MoU, emphasizing that the United States has a responsibility to actively contribute to ending the war and stopping hostilities on all fronts, including in Lebanon.
​
He also pointed out the opportunities for enhancing relations between Iran and France, particularly in the economic and commercial sectors, that have arisen from the Islamabad MoU.
​
Araghchi underscored the need for decisive and comprehensive support from the international community and international organizations, such as the United Nations Security Council, to ensure the implementation of this MoU and to support the peaceful processes it generates.
​
The two sides also emphasized the importance of safe and secure transit and shipping in compliance with international law in the Strait of Hormuz.
